headline: Resort and Forest Stays: Girdwood Lodging Verification
reservation: Girdwood accommodations, including glamping and resort stays, require advance booking due to high seasonal demand. Local forest service cabins are managed through a separate federal lottery or reservation system; always check the official Chugach National Forest and Alaska State Parks websites for current permit requirements.

days.title: Glacial Valleys and Coastal Views
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Girdwood Town Center

stops.name: Alyeska Aerial Tramway
stops.detail: Ascend to 2,300 feet for panoramic views of Turnagain Arm and seven hanging glaciers.

stops.name: North Face Trail
stops.detail: Hike the steep terrain up the mountain or use the walking paths at the summit for alpine air.

days.driving: Local transfer; allow 15 minutes between town and the resort base.
days.note: Tram operations are weather-dependent; high winds can cause temporary service suspensions.

days.title: Rainforest Canopy and Rushing Gorges

stops.name: Winner Creek Trail
stops.detail: Walk through a temperate rainforest of ancient hemlock and spruce to reach the Winner Creek gorge.

stops.name: Roundhouse at Alyeska Museum
stops.detail: Explore the local history and ski culture housed in a historic octagonal building at the mountain top.

days.driving: Local transfer; allow walking time from town to the trailhead.
days.note: The Winner Creek hand tram is closed. Plan an out-and-back walk and do not rely on it to cross the gorge; check Forest Service updates before hiking.

days.title: Coastal Tides and Marine Wildlife

stops.name: Bird Point
stops.detail: Scan the Turnagain Arm for Beluga whales and observe the dramatic bore tide wave.

stops.name: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center
stops.detail: See orphaned or injured Alaskan species including wood bison, bears, and moose in a natural setting.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the scenic drive along Turnagain Arm; conditions vary.
days.note: Bore tide timing is specific to the lunar cycle; consult local tide tables for sightings.

intel.title: Winter Road Safety
intel.text: The Seward Highway is prone to avalanches and closures during heavy snow. Check the Alaska 511 system for current road status between Anchorage and Girdwood.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Refuel in Girdwood before heading south to the Kenai Peninsula. The next reliable service stations are in Whittier or further south toward Seward.

intel.title: Valley Coverage
intel.text: Service is generally strong in the Girdwood valley but drops off rapidly on backcountry trails. Carry physical maps for the Chugach National Forest.

intel.title: Midnight Sun Daylight
intel.text: In June and July, daylight lasts nearly 20 hours, allowing for late-evening activities. Pace yourself to avoid exhaustion despite the lack of darkness.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Winner Creek parking fills quickly on summer weekends. Utilize the resort overflow lots if the main trailhead area is occupied.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Anchorage (ANC), drive south via the Seward Highway, and check into valley lodging before exploring the resort base.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for town access; winter visits require 4WD and winter-rated tires.
plan.goldenHour: Bird Point offers reflections of the Chugach Mountains at dusk; seasonal timing ranges from 4 PM in winter to 11 PM in summer.
